title: Updated code to use class based approach for treemap
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

This pull request refactors the `TreeMapDB` implementation in the `mermaid` package, transitioning from a static object-based database to a class-based structure.


Resolves #6692

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body:
This is an antipattern for class based diagrams. 
The class itself does the purpose of ImperativeState, and ImperativeState was designed to manage _all_ state, so having `data` outside breaks that pattern. 

For class based diagrams, we just have to write everything as members of the class directly. No need to use ImperativeState, or a `data` object.

comments.author: aloisklink

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
**nitpick**: I don't like using `as XXXXXX` unless we know with 100% certainty that the type is correct.

Is there any reason why we can't just make an empty `TreemapDB` for this?

```suggestion
  parser: { yy: new TreemapDB() },
```

Or if you really want to leave it with some default value, maybe

```suggestion
  // @ts-expect-error: Will be replaced with a real DB during init
  parser: { yy: undefined },
```

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: We were using `undefined` with `// @ts-expect-error:` yesterday, that should be done.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags use of `as XXXXXX` as bad practice and provides two concrete alternative suggestions.

comments.author: aloisklink

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Provides a concrete code suggestion to replace unsafe `as` cast with an instanceof check and proper error message.
Directly requests a specific code change: use `undefined` with `ts-expect-error` instead of the current approach.
